results.title: Polycyclic group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is polycyclic if for some $n \ge 0$ there are subgroups $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \cdots \le H_n = G$ such that for each $i < n$, $H_i$ is normal in $H_{i+1}$ and the quotient $H_{i+1} / H_i$ is cyclic.

results.title: Almost polycyclic group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is almost polycyclic (polycyclic-by-finite) if it has a subgroup of finite index that is polycyclic.

results.title: Artamonov's freeness question (Kourovka 11.5)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: This is the proposition that, for every commutative ring $k$, every torsion-free almost polycyclic group $G$ (no element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has finite order) and every finitely generated projective module $P$ over the group ring $kG$, if $P$ contains two elements that are linearly independent over $kG$, then $P$ is a free $kG$-module.

results.title: Artamonov's freeness question has a negative answer
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not the case that for every commutative ring $k$, every torsion-free almost polycyclic group $G$ (no element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ has finite order) and every finitely generated projective module $P$ over the group ring $kG$ containing two elements that are linearly independent over $kG$, the module $P$ is free over $kG$.

path: Differential geometry of curves and surfaces

results.title: Euclidean 3-space for the Fáry–Milnor theorem
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: Euclidean 3-space is the real vector space $\mathbb{R}^3$ with the Euclidean inner product and norm.

results.title: Period of a parametrised knot
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The period used for parametrised knots is the real number $2\pi$.

results.title: Velocity of a space curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $t$, the velocity of $r$ at $t$ is its derivative $r'(t)$, taken to be $0$ when $r$ is not differentiable at $t$.

results.title: Acceleration of a space curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ and a real number $t$, the acceleration of $r$ at $t$ is the derivative at $t$ of its velocity $s \mapsto r'(s)$, that is $r''(t)$, where a derivative that does not exist is taken to be $0$.

results.title: Curvature of a space curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with velocity $r'$ and acceleration $r''$, the curvature of $r$ at a real number $t$ is $\kappa(t) = \lVert r'(t) \times r''(t) \rVert / \lVert r'(t) \rVert^3$, where $\times$ is the cross product and $\lVert \cdot \rVert$ is the Euclidean norm; the quotient is $0$ when $r'(t) = 0$.

results.title: Total curvature of a space curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ with velocity $r'$ and curvature $\kappa$, the total curvature of $r$ is the arc-length integral $\int_0^{2\pi} \kappa(t) \, \lVert r'(t) \rVert \, dt$ over one period, where the integral is taken to be $0$ if the integrand is not integrable.

results.title: Standard circle
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The standard circle is the curve $\mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ given by $t \mapsto (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$: the unit circle centred at the origin in the $xy$-plane.

results.title: Smooth knot
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is a smooth knot when it is real-analytic, periodic with period $2\pi$, injective on $[0, 2\pi)$, and regular, that is, its velocity $r'(t)$ is nonzero for every real number $t$.

results.title: Unknotted curve
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A curve $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ is unknotted when there is a real-analytic map $R \colon \mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ such that $R(t, 0) = r(t)$ and $R(t, 1) = (\cos t, \sin t, 0)$, the standard circle, for every real number $t$, and for every $s \in [0, 1]$ the curve $t \mapsto R(t, s)$ is a smooth knot.

results.title: Fáry–Milnor theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $r \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}^3$ be a smooth knot, that is, a real-analytic, $2\pi$-periodic curve that is injective on $[0, 2\pi)$ and has nonzero velocity everywhere. If the total curvature of $r$ is at most $4\pi$, then $r$ is unknotted: there is a real-analytic isotopy from $r$ to the standard circle through smooth knots.

results.title: The torus of period $2\pi$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The two-dimensional torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, the product of two copies of the circle $\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Integer frequencies
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: The frequencies are the elements of the lattice $\mathbb{Z}^2$, that is, the pairs $k = (k_1, k_2)$ of integers; they index the Fourier modes of the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.

results.title: Rescaling the torus to unit period
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The homeomorphism from the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ onto the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ that sends $(x_1, x_2)$ to $(x_1/(2\pi), x_2/(2\pi))$.

results.title: A function on the torus as a function on the unit torus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a continuous function $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its unit representative is the continuous function $\tilde u : (\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{C}$ given by $\tilde u(y) = u(2\pi y)$, the composition of $u$ with the inverse of the rescaling to unit period, with its real values regarded as complex numbers.

results.title: Fourier coefficients on the torus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ be continuous and let $k \in \mathbb{Z}^2$ be a frequency. The Fourier coefficient of $u$ at $k$ is $a_k = 2\pi c_k$, where $c_k = \int_{[0,1]^2} u(2\pi y)\, e^{-2\pi i\, k \cdot y}\, dy$ is the Fourier coefficient of the rescaled function $y \mapsto u(2\pi y)$ on the unit torus with respect to normalized Haar measure. Equivalently,…

results.title: Squared frequency
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a frequency $k = (k_1, k_2) \in \mathbb{Z}^2$, the frequency weight is $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$, the squared frequency of the mode $e^{i k \cdot x}$ on the torus $(\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$.

results.title: Gradient energy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the gradient energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^2 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.

results.title: Laplacian energy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$, the Laplacian energy is $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} |k|^4 \, |a_k|^2$, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$; the sum is taken to be $0$ when the series diverges.

results.title: Functions in $H^2$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ with Fourier coefficients $a_k$ is in $H^2$ when the series $\sum_{k \in \mathbb{Z}^2} (1 + |k|^2)^2 \, |a_k|^2$ converges, where $|k|^2 = k_1^2 + k_2^2$.

results.title: Normalized Haar measure on the unit torus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The measure on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ that is the product of two copies of the Haar probability measure on the circle $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

results.title: Mean of a function on the torus
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a continuous function $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$, its mean is $\int_{(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2} u(2\pi y)\, d\mu(y)$, where $\mu$ is the normalized Haar measure on the unit torus $(\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z})^2$ and $y \mapsto 2\pi y$ is the inverse of the rescaling to unit period.

results.title: Zero-mean $H^2$ functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is a zero-mean $H^2$ function when it is in $H^2$ and its mean is $0$.

results.title: Conditionally admissible functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\delta$ be a real number. A continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ is admissible at level $\delta$ when it is a zero-mean $H^2$ function, its gradient energy equals $1$, and its Laplacian energy equals $\delta$.

results.title: Squared values at the origin of admissible functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $\delta$, this is the set of extended real numbers $u(0)^2$, where $u$ ranges over the continuous functions $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ that are conditionally admissible at level $\delta$.

results.title: Conditional supremum of the squared value at the origin
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real $\delta$, $\theta(\delta)$ is the supremum, taken in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the conditional point values at $\delta$: the numbers $u(0)^2$ over all continuous $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that are conditionally admissible at $\delta$, that is, of mean zero and in $H^2$ with gradient energy $1$ and Laplace energy $\delta$.

results.title: Frequency ratio
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a continuous function $u : (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2 \to \mathbb{R}$, the frequency ratio is the Laplacian energy of $u$ divided by the gradient energy of $u$.

results.title: Logarithmic remainder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For real $\delta$, the remainder is the extended real number $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$, where $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

results.title: Set of remainder values
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The set of extended real numbers $R(\delta)$ for all real $\delta \ge 1$, where $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$ is the logarithmic remainder and $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

results.title: Sharp logarithmic remainder
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sharp remainder is the supremum, in the extended reals $[-\infty, \infty]$, of the remainders $R(\delta) = 4\pi\,\theta(\delta) - \log \delta - \log(1 + \log \delta)$ over all real $\delta \ge 1$, where $\theta(\delta)$ is the conditional supremum of $u(0)^2$ over the functions conditionally admissible at $\delta$.

results.title: Uniform logarithmic remainder bound
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real constant $L$, the bound with constant $L$ holds when, for every continuous $u : \mathbb{T}^2 \to \mathbb{R}$ on the torus $\mathbb{T}^2 = (\mathbb{R}/2\pi\mathbb{Z})^2$ that has mean zero and lies in $H^2$, has positive gradient energy $E(u)$, and, writing $\Delta(u)$ for its Laplace energy, has frequency ratio $\Lambda(u) = \Delta(u)/E(u) \ge 1$, every point $x$ of the torus satisfies…

results.title: Start of a run
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Position $i$ of a word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ of natural numbers starts a run when $i = 0$ or the letter before it is larger, that is, $w_{i-1} > w_i$. Runs are the maximal contiguous weakly increasing subwords, so these are exactly the positions where a run begins.

results.title: Number of runs of a word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A run of a word $w = w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{m-1}$ of natural numbers is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword. The number of runs of $w$ is the number of positions $i < m$ that start a run, that is, with $i = 0$ or $w_{i-1} > w_i$; the empty word has no runs.

results.title: Flattened words
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A word $w = w_1 w_2 \cdots w_m$ of natural numbers is flattened when the leading letters of its runs, read left to right, are weakly increasing. Here a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword, so position $i$ starts a run when $i = 1$ or $w_{i-1} > w_i$; the condition is that $w_i \le w_j$ whenever $i < j$ and both positions start runs.

results.title: Number of flattened Stirling permutations
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, $|\mathrm{flat}(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$: words $w_1 w_2 \cdots w_{2n}$ of natural numbers that are Stirling permutations of order $n$ and whose runs (maximal contiguous weakly increasing subwords) have weakly increasing leading letters, read from left to right.

results.title: Counting flattened Stirling permutations by runs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, $|\mathrm{flat}_k(Q_n)|$ is the number of flattened Stirling permutations of order $n$ with exactly $k$ runs, where a run is a maximal contiguous weakly increasing subword.

results.title: Flattened partitions counted by runs

results.title: Type $B$ set partitions

results.title: Exponential generating function of the Dowling numbers
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $n \ge 0$ let $D_n$ be the $n$-th Dowling number of the group of order $2$, that is, the $(q, r)$-Dowling number $D_n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} W_{2,1,1}(n, k)$ built from the $(q, r)$-Whitney numbers of the second kind with $m = 2$, $r = 1$, $q = 1$. Then for every complex number $x$ the series $\sum_{n \ge 0} D_n x^n / n!$ is summable with sum $\exp\bigl(x + (e^{2x} - 1)/2\bigr)$.

results.title: The shift map
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $S$ of integers, $h(S) = \{|i| + 1 : i \in S\}$, a finite set of natural numbers.

results.title: Doubled word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\}$ of natural numbers, the doubled word of $S$ is $f(S) = s_1 s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k$, which lists the elements of $S$ in increasing order with each one written twice; $f(\emptyset)$ is the empty word.

results.title: Wrapped word of a finite set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $S = \{s_1 < s_2 < \dots < s_k\}$ of natural numbers, the wrapped word $g(S)$ is $s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k s_1$: the smallest element, then each larger element written twice in increasing order, then the smallest element again. For $S = \emptyset$, $g(S)$ is the empty word.

results.title: An example of the shift map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the map $h(S) = \{|i| + 1 : i \in S\}$ on finite sets of integers, $h(\{-2, 0, 1\}) = \{1, 2, 3\}$.

results.title: The doubled word of a singleton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s$, the doubled word of the singleton $\{s\}$ is $f(\{s\}) = s\,s$, the word of length two whose letters are both $s$.

results.title: Length of the doubled word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $S$ of natural numbers with elements $s_1 < \dots < s_k$, the doubled word $f(S) = s_1 s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k$ has length $2|S|$.

results.title: Wrapped word of the empty set
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The wrapped word $g(\emptyset)$ of the empty set is the empty word.

results.title: Wrapped word of a singleton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $s$, the wrapped word of the singleton $\{s\}$ is $g(\{s\}) = s\,s$, the word of length two both of whose letters are $s$.

results.title: Length of the wrapped word
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every finite set $S$ of natural numbers with elements $s_1 < \dots < s_k$, the wrapped word $g(S) = s_1 s_2 s_2 \cdots s_k s_k s_1$ (the empty word when $S = \emptyset$) has length $2|S|$.

results.title: Adler labels lie in $\{1, \dots, n\}$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every set partition $P$ of $\{-n, \dots, n\}$, every Adler block label $p$ of $P$ is an integer with $1 \le p \le n$.

results.title: Truncated subset expansion of parity products modulo powers of two

results.title: Uniform hypergraphs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform when every edge $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.

results.title: Subhypergraph containment
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$, viewed as a hypergraph with edge set $H$, and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges when there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ edges of $H$ are subsets of $S$.

results.title: Characterization of uniform hypergraphs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $r \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ is $r$-uniform if and only if every member $e \in H$ has exactly $r$ elements.

results.title: Characterization of subhypergraph containment
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $H$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $V$ and let $m, k \in \mathbb{N}$. Then $H$ contains a subgraph with $m$ vertices and at least $k$ edges if and only if there is a set $S$ of exactly $m$ elements of $V$ such that at least $k$ members of $H$ are subsets of $S$.

results.title: Intersecting families
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting when every two distinct members meet: for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.

results.title: Characterization of intersecting families

results.summary: Let $F$ be a finite family of finite subsets of a type $\alpha$. Then $F$ is intersecting if and only if for all $A, B \in F$ with $A \neq B$, the intersection $A \cap B$ is nonempty.

results.title: Halting of a single-tape machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A single-tape Turing machine $M$ halts on an input word $l$ when its run, started in its start state with $l$ on the tape, reaches a halting configuration.

results.title: Halting agrees with evaluation for multi-stack machines

results.summary: A multi-stack machine halts on a word $l$ over the alphabet of its input stack if and only if the evaluation of its transition function, started at its main label and initial internal state with $l$ on the input stack and all other stacks empty, is defined.

results.title: Satisfaction of a DNF formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A DNF formula is a list of terms, each a list of literals $(v, b)$ of a natural number $v$ (the variable) and a boolean $b$ (the polarity). An assignment $a$ of booleans to the natural numbers satisfies the formula when some term of it has $a(v) = b$ for every literal $(v, b)$ of that term.

results.title: Number of satisfying assignments of an encoded DNF formula

results.title: Membership in a binary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A key $x$ belongs to a binary tree $T$ when it is the key of some node of $T$: no key belongs to the empty tree, and $x$ belongs to a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ exactly when $x$ belongs to $L$, $x = k$, or $x$ belongs to $R$.

results.title: Inorder traversal of a binary tree with an accumulator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a list $s$, the accumulated traversal of the empty tree onto $s$ is $s$, and the accumulated traversal of a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ onto $s$ is the accumulated traversal of $L$ onto the list consisting of $k$ followed by the accumulated traversal of $R$ onto $s$.

results.title: Inorder traversal of a binary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The inorder traversal of a binary tree $t$ is the accumulated inorder traversal of $t$ onto the empty list. Equivalently, the empty tree gives the empty list, and a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ gives the inorder traversal of $L$, then $k$, then the inorder traversal of $R$.

results.title: A predicate holding at every key of a binary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a predicate $p$ on a type $\alpha$, the empty binary tree satisfies "every key satisfies $p$", and a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ satisfies it exactly when $L$ satisfies it, $p(k)$ holds and $R$ satisfies it.

results.title: Ordered binary trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a relation $<$. The empty tree is ordered, and a binary tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ is ordered when $L$ and $R$ are ordered, every key of $L$ is less than $k$, and $k$ is less than every key of $R$.

results.title: Search in a binary search tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the search for $x$ in $t$ returns a Boolean: false if $t$ is empty, and if $t$ is a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the search for $x$ in $L$ when $x < k$, the search for $x$ in $R$ when $k < x$, and true otherwise.

results.title: Insertion into a binary search tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, inserting $x$ into the empty tree gives the single node with key $x$ and empty subtrees; inserting $x$ into a node with key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ inserts $x$ into $L$ when $x < k$, inserts $x$ into $R$ when $k < x$, and returns the node unchanged when $x = k$.

results.title: Rank of a key in a binary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the rank of $x$ in $t$ is the number of positions of the inorder traversal of $t$ whose entry is strictly less than $x$.

results.title: Inorder selection in a binary tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a natural number $i$, selecting index $i$ in $t$ returns the entry at zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of $t$ when $i$ is less than the length of that traversal, and returns nothing otherwise.

results.title: Binary search tree built from a list
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, the binary tree built from a list $[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ of elements of $\alpha$ is obtained from the empty tree by inserting $x_n$, then $x_{n-1}$, and so on down to $x_1$, using binary search tree insertion; the empty list gives the empty tree.

results.title: A predicate holds at all keys of a binary tree iff it holds at all its members
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$, a predicate $p$ on $\alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, every key of $t$ satisfies $p$ in the recursive sense (the empty tree qualifies, and a node qualifies when its left subtree qualifies, its key satisfies $p$ and its right subtree qualifies) if and only if $p(x)$ holds for every $x$ that is a member of $t$.

results.title: Membership in the inorder traversal of a binary tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary tree $T$ and every key $x$, $x$ occurs in the inorder traversal of $T$ if and only if $x$ lies in $T$.

results.title: Membership after insertion into a binary search tree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered. For all keys $x, y$ and every binary tree $T$, $y$ lies in the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ if and only if $y = x$ or $y$ lies in $T$.

results.title: Binary search tree insertion preserves order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every key $x \in \alpha$ and every ordered binary tree $T$ over $\alpha$, the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ is ordered.

results.title: Search in a binary search tree is correct
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$ that is ordered (recursively, every key in the left subtree of a node is strictly smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is strictly larger), the comparison search for $x$ in $t$ returns true if and only if $x$ is a member of $t$.

results.title: The inorder traversal of an ordered binary tree is strictly increasing
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. If a binary tree $T$ over $\alpha$ is ordered, then in the inorder traversal of $T$ every key is less than every key that comes after it.

results.title: The inorder traversal of a binary search tree has no duplicates
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$ that is ordered (recursively, every key in the left subtree of a node is strictly smaller than the node's key and every key in its right subtree is strictly larger), the inorder traversal of $t$ is a list with no repeated entries.

results.title: Binary search trees built from a list are ordered
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type. For every list $xs$ of elements of $\alpha$, the tree obtained from the empty tree by inserting the elements of $xs$ one at a time, from the last element to the first, is ordered.

results.title: Members of the binary search tree built from a list
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a list $xs$ of elements of $\alpha$, $x$ is a member of the binary tree built from $xs$ by successive binary search tree insertion if and only if $x$ occurs in $xs$.

results.title: The length of the inorder traversal of a binary tree is its number of nodes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every binary tree $T$, the number of nodes of $T$ (each node carries one key, and the empty tree has none) equals the length of the inorder traversal of $T$.

results.title: Inserting a present key into a binary search tree leaves its size unchanged
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered, and let $T$ be an ordered binary tree. If a key $x$ lies in $T$, then the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ has the same number of nodes as $T$.

results.title: Inserting an absent key into a binary search tree adds one node
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let the keys be linearly ordered. For every binary tree $T$ and every key $x$ that does not lie in $T$, the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ has one more node than $T$.

results.title: Rank counts the smaller inorder entries
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a linearly ordered type $\alpha$, a key $x \in \alpha$ and a binary tree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, the rank of $x$ in $t$ equals the length of the list obtained from the inorder traversal of $t$ by keeping exactly the entries strictly less than $x$.

results.title: Selection is indexing into the inorder traversal
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a binary tree $t$ and a natural number $i$, selecting index $i$ in $t$ gives the same result as looking up zero-based position $i$ of the inorder traversal of $t$: the entry at that position when $i$ is less than the length of the traversal, and nothing otherwise.

results.title: Selecting the rank of a key returns the key
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $t$ be a binary search tree with keys in $\alpha$, that is, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger than the node's key. If $x$ is a key of $t$, then selecting, in $t$, the index equal to the rank of $x$ in $t$ returns $x$.

results.title: The rank of a selected key is its index
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a linearly ordered type and let $t$ be a binary search tree with keys in $\alpha$, that is, at every node each key of the left subtree is strictly smaller and each key of the right subtree is strictly larger than the node's key. If selecting index $i$ in $t$ returns a key $x$, then the rank of $x$ in $t$ equals $i$.

results.title: Join of two binary trees
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The join of the empty tree and a tree $R$ is $R$. The join of a tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L_1$ and right subtree $L_2$ and a tree $R$ is the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L_1$ and right subtree the join of $L_2$ and $R$. Thus, when the first tree is nonempty, $R$ becomes the right subtree of its rightmost node.

results.title: Deletion from a binary search tree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x$ be a key of a linearly ordered type. Deleting $x$ from the empty tree gives the empty tree. Deleting $x$ from a tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ gives the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ with $x$ deleted and right subtree $R$ if $x < k$; the tree with root key $k$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$ with $x$ deleted if $k < x$; and the join of $L$ and $R$…

results.title: Membership in a join
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary trees $L$ and $R$, a key $x$ occurs in the join of $L$ and $R$ if and only if $x$ occurs in $L$ or $x$ occurs in $R$.

results.title: Inorder traversal of a join
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For binary trees $L$ and $R$, the inorder traversal of the join of $L$ and $R$ is the inorder traversal of $L$ followed by the inorder traversal of $R$.

results.title: Joining separated ordered trees
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L$ and $R$ be ordered binary search trees over a type with a relation $<$. If $a < b$ for every key $a$ of $L$ and every key $b$ of $R$, then the join of $L$ and $R$ is ordered.

results.title: Deletion keeps the other keys
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $t$ be a binary tree over a linearly ordered type, not necessarily ordered, and let $x$ and $y$ be keys with $y \ne x$. If $y$ occurs in $t$, then $y$ occurs in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$.

results.title: The deleted key is gone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type and $x$ is a key, then $x$ does not occur in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$.

results.title: Membership after deletion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type, then for all keys $x$ and $y$, the key $y$ occurs in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ if and only if $y$ occurs in $t$ and $y \ne x$.

results.title: Deletion preserves the search-tree order
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type, then for every key $x$ the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ is ordered.

results.title: Inorder traversal after deletion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $t$ is an ordered binary search tree over a linearly ordered type and $x$ is a key, then the inorder traversal of the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $t$ is the inorder traversal of $t$ with the first occurrence of $x$ removed (and is the inorder traversal of $t$ itself if $x$ does not occur in it).
